steps.prompt: In a counting problem, how do you decide whether order matters?

cards.title: The counting toolkit
cards.body: Multiply independent choices. Order matters: permutations. Order doesn't matter: $\binom{n}{k}$. Identical objects into boxes: stars and bars, $\binom{n + k - 1}{k - 1}$. "At least one": count the complement. Overlaps: inclusion–exclusion. Probability is favourable over total, with equally likely outcomes.

cards.title: The number theory toolkit
cards.body: Factor into primes first. $n = p^a q^b$ has $(a + 1)(b + 1)$ divisors. $\gcd \times \operatorname{lcm} = $ the product of the two numbers. Remainders multiply and add: work mod $m$ from the start. Units digits and remainders of powers repeat in cycles.

cards.title: Worked example: a cycle
cards.problem: What is the remainder when $2^{100}$ is divided by $5$?

steps.text: The remainders of $2, 4, 8, 16$ are $2, 4, 3, 1$: a cycle of length $4$.
$100$ is a multiple of $4$, so the remainder is that of $2^4$: $1$.
